editorial:
Imagine moving to a rainy, gray town in Oregon where everyone seems a bit off. You follow a teacher who tries to help a quiet young boy, but she soon realizes he is hiding something truly scary. Her brother, the local sheriff, is also struggling with his own demons, which makes the whole town feel heavy and tense. It starts as a slow mystery about a kid in trouble, but it quickly turns into a nightmare involving an ancient monster that feeds on people's pain and guilt. The atmosphere is thick, and you will feel the dread building up as the characters get closer to the truth.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the leads bring a lot of real emotion to the screen. While the middle part drags a bit, the creature effects at the end are impressive and creepy. If you like movies that mix family drama with monsters, you will enjoy this one.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big fight against the Wendigo monster. You find out the creature uses people's grief to take over their bodies. The teacher eventually manages to kill the beast, but not before it causes a lot of death. The story wraps up with the survivors dealing with their loss, showing that while the monster is gone, the emotional scars they carry will stay with them forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster movies with a sad story.
